document.description: The plan document reference: a lowercase name like "sprint-42", never a path.

title.description: The new session title; meaningful only with act "retitle".

relations.relation_purpose: Enact one custody-native act on an existing plan document: undo the last revision, redo an undone one, or retitle the session. Answers nothing-to-undo, nothing-to-redo, or document-absent as named results.

document.description: The plan document reference: a lowercase name like "sprint-42", never a path.

limit.description: Window size; meaningful for present, session-tasks, revisions.

offset.description: Window start; meaningful for present, session-tasks, revisions.

unit_id.description: The unit to detail; meaningful only with window "unit-detail".

relations.relation_purpose: Read one windowed projection of a plan document: present (compact unit summaries, relation endpoints, semantic labels), unit-detail (one unit in full), session-tasks, revisions, or undo-horizon. Reads never create a document; an absent one answers document-absent.

command.description: Exactly one task in the game command grammar.

document.description: The plan document reference: a lowercase name like "sprint-42", never a path.

focus.description: Optional comma-separated unit ids narrowing how references in the command resolve.

relations.relation_purpose:
Submit exactly one task against a plan document, written in the game command grammar (version 2). If the named document does not exist yet, a realized task births it; a refused task births nothing. A refusal comes back as a named result (for example unrecognized-verb, unknown-node, ambiguous-reference, malformed-argument, dependency-cycle), never as an error. Use focus (comma-separated unit ids) when a name in the command could resolve to more than one unit. The commands:
create game "G" — Starts a new top-level game with that goal. Example: create game "Ship v1"
add method "D" to <ref> — Gives a game a method describing how it will be pursued. Example: add method "Build the prototype" to "Ship v1"
add game "G" under <ref> — Opens a sub-game beneath an existing method. Example: add game "Ship the beta" under "Ship v1"
add task "T" to <ref> — Adds a unit of work beneath a method. Example: add task "Draft the schema" to "Ship v1"
add criterion "C" to <ref> — Adds an acceptance criterion to a unit. Example: add criterion "Tests pass" to "Draft the schema"
add measure "N" to <ref> baseline B target T unit "U" — Attaches a quantitative measure with its baseline and target. Example: add measure "Latency" to "Ship v1" baseline 400 target 100 unit "ms"
revise goal of <ref> to "G" — Restates what a game is for. Example: revise goal of "Ship v1" to "Ship v2"
set explanation of <ref> to "E" — Records the reasoning behind a unit. Example: set explanation of "Ship v1" to "Why this matters now"
set owner of <ref> to "O" — Names who is accountable for a unit. Example: set owner of "Draft the schema" to "Ada"
set status of <ref> to <status> — Moves a unit along its lifecycle. Example: set status of "Draft the schema" to active
set priority of <ref> to N — Orders a unit against its siblings. Example: set priority of "Draft the schema" to 2
set forecast of <ref> to P L G — Records a pessimistic, likely and good-case forecast. Example: set forecast of "Ship v1" to 2026-01-01 2026-02-01 2026-03-01
set measure "N" of <ref> to X — Updates a measure to its current reading. Example: set measure "Latency" of "Ship v1" to 250
mark criterion "C" of <ref> satisfied — Declares an acceptance criterion met. Example: mark criterion "Tests pass" of "Draft the schema" satisfied
link <ref> depends on <ref> — Records that one unit depends on another. Example: link "Ship the beta" depends on "Draft the schema"
unlink <ref> from <ref> — Removes a dependency between two units. Example: unlink "Ship the beta" from "Draft the schema"

exposition.tool_purpose: Plan documents as an agent capability: submit grammar tasks, direct custody (undo, redo, retitle), and read windowed projections. Every act crosses the plan contract exactly as a human act would.

state.purpose: The plan documents themselves: each key is one plan document reference, each document one persisted .game artifact. Permanent because plans outlive any single mandate.
